topic: What if your shadow was always 3 seconds behind you?
title: WHAT IF YOUR SHADOW
WAS 3 SECONDS LATE?

script.beat: 1 cold open: three demos of the delay
script.text: You jump. You land. Then your shadow jumps. You trip on the stairs. You get back up. Your shadow is still falling. You wave at your crush. She waves back. Your shadow waves. Three seconds later.
What if your shadow was always three seconds behind you?
At first, it's the best party trick ever. You dance, and your shadow does the replay. Your friends lose it. You go viral.
Here's the thing. Shadows are already made of old light. Sunlight is eight minutes old when it hits you. That's real. Yours is just a little older.
Then a man in a suit knocks on your door. He wants to study it.
And one morning, it happens. Your shadow moves first. It reaches for your little sister. And you haven't moved at all.
Part one. Would you follow your shadow, or run? Tell me in the comments.

science.claim: Sunlight is about 8 minutes old when it reaches you.
science.working: Earth-Sun distance ~149.6 million km / speed of light 299,792 km/s = ~499 s = 8 min 19 s.
science.source: NASA, 'How long does it take sunlight to reach Earth?'
